title: Fix largeParquet gitignore so git clean -fd stops wiping it
description:
I seemed to have messed this up previously...

PR #151 added `/data-files/largeParquet.parquet` to `workspaces/r_testing/.gitignore`, but the file is downloaded at e2e runtime to the repo-root `data-files/` directory, not under `workspaces/r_testing/`. A nested .gitignore only governs its own subtree, and the leading `/` anchored the rule to the nonexistent `workspaces/r_testing/data-files/`, so the rule never matched.

The untracked parquet therefore stayed un-ignored, and a concurrent e2e worker's `discardAllChanges()` teardown (`git reset --hard` + `git clean -fd`) wiped it mid-suite. The R "very large data frame" test then failed with `IOError: Failed to open ... largeParquet.parquet: No such file`.

Move the ignore to the root .gitignore (matching the real download path) and drop the stale r_testing entry.

title: server: update tests for server verifier
description:
## Set up Positron license-token minting for the local Jupyter/TLJH stack

### Summary

Moves the local jupyter-local Docker stack from handing the raw Positron .lic to user sessions over to a per-session token-minting flow. 

`jupyter-positron-server` and `jupyter-positron-verifier` install github, will need updated after everything lands in `positron-builds`

### Changes

`install-jupyter-positron.sh`
- License flow rework: the .lic is now entitlement only — read by the Hub verifier (via license-manager), not by user sessions.
- Minting service install: installs jupyter-positron-verifier into the TLJH hub env (/opt/tljh/hub).
- Signing key: installs the out-of-band signing key to /etc/positron/signing-key.pem (chmod 600). It must pair with the `OrchestratorPublicKey` embedded in positron https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/14260
- JupyterHub config: writes `positron-minting.py` (registers the positron-license managed service on port 10101 with a read:users role) and `positron-env.py` (points sessions at the minting endpoint via POSITRON_LICENSE_MINTING_ENDPOINT).
- Branch-build support: adds POSITRON_SERVER_TARBALL so CI can install positron-server from a pre-staged branch tarball instead of a published positron-builds release, falling back to download when unset/missing. It looks like we were building from a branch, but then testing against the nightly build

`connect.sh`
- Copies ./signing-key.pem into the container staging area (/opt/signing-key.pem) via docker cp

`.gitignore`
- Ignores signing-key.pem so the key is never committed.

title: Add largeParquet to gitignore
description:
Positron's very-large-data-frame.test.ts downloads data-files/largeParquet.parquet from S3 at runtime into the shared e2e workspace (this repo). The file is untracked and not ignored.

Because all 3 e2e workers share one workspace directory, a concurrent test's teardown (git clean -fd) deletes this untracked file mid-run. The result is an intermittent IOError: Failed to open local file '.../largeParquet.parquet' ... No such file or directory in the data-explorer performance tests — the fixture downloads fine, then gets wiped before the next test reads it.

Adding it to .gitignore fixes this: git clean -fd (no -x) skips ignored files, so the download survives.

title: Managed Credentials Flag for Workbench
description:
## Summary

Workbench local setup now configures **one** credential type per install, selected
with a `--credentials=<databricks|snowflake|azure>` flag, instead of auto-configuring
every data source whose env vars happen to be present. Adds Azure (Entra ID / OpenID)
support and fixes a bug where flags passed via `npm run wb:connect` were silently dropped.

## Changes

- **`configure-datasources.sh`** — rewritten to take the credential type as an argument
  and configure exactly one source via a `case`:
  - `databricks` — writes `databricks.conf`, sets `databricks-enabled=1`
  - `snowflake` — writes `snowflake.conf`, sets `allow-refresh-snowflake-roles=1`
  - `azure` (new) — appends the OpenID block to `rserver.conf`, creates
    `/etc/rstudio/openid-client-secret` (`chmod 0600`), and adds `pam_mkhomedir.so`
    to `/etc/pam.d/common-session` for JIT-provisioned home dirs
  - Errors if the required secret is missing; all file appends are idempotent.

- **`install-workbench.sh`** — parses/validates `--credentials`, logs the selection,
  and passes it through to `configure-datasources.sh`. No flag → no data source configured.

- **`connect.sh`** — parses/validates `--credentials`, documents it in `--help`, logs
  the selected type early, passes `AZURE_SERVICE_PRINCIPAL_CLIENT_SECRET` into the
  container, and forwards the flag in both CI and interactive paths.

- **`package.json`** — fixed `wb:connect` to forward args (`"$@"`) so
  `npm run wb:connect -- --credentials=...` (and `--ci`) actually reach `connect.sh`.

- **`.env.example` / `README.md`** — added `AZURE_SERVICE_PRINCIPAL_CLIENT_SECRET` and
  documented the `--credentials` flag with a per-type requirements table.

## Usage

```bash
GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_... npm run wb:connect -- --credentials=azure
# or directly:
GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_... ./connect.sh --credentials=snowflake

title: Add `r-session-hooks` workspace (`.Rprofile` + `DESCRIPTION`)
description:
Adds `.Rprofile` with `positron.session_init` and `positron.session_reconnect` hooks for E2E testing (posit-dev/positron#12802).

### Background

`.Rprofile` is an R startup file executed automatically when a session starts. Users use it to configure options, load packages, and customize IDE behavior; this can be of very high-value for R users transitioning to Positron.

### What this adds

A dedicated workspace with an `.Rprofile` that exercises session hooks and a `DESCRIPTION` file used as a `navigateToFile()` target. The profile validates:

- Hook firing with correct `start_type` across new, restart, and reconnect flows
- Console width propagation (`options("width")` and `cli::console_width()`)
- Two-way `rstudioapi` communication inside hooks (`getActiveProject()`, `navigateToFile("DESCRIPTION")`)

### QA Hot Points 🌶️

- E2E tests should verify expected console output, correct hook firing behavior, and that `DESCRIPTION` opens via `rstudioapi::navigateToFile()`.
- This `.Rprofile` was intentionally added in a dedicated subfolder rather than the global `qa-example-content` root to avoid affecting unrelated QA workflows and startup behavior. 
  - Since `.Rprofile` files are automatically executed at R session startup, keeping this isolated ensures the hook-based lifecycle testing only applies to scenarios that explicitly opt into it.

title: Managed cred setup for workbench container
description:
# Add Databricks and Snowflake configuration support to wb-local
Adds support for configuring Databricks and Snowflake connections in the Workbench local development environment via environment variables.

# Changes
New script: configure-datasources.sh - Configures Databricks and Snowflake connections for Workbench
Updated: install-workbench.sh - Calls the configuration script during installation
Updated: connect.sh - Forwards environment variables from .env file into the container
## Environment Variables
Add these to your dockerfiles/wb-local/.env file:


### Databricks
DATABRICKS_URL=
DATABRICKS_CLIENT_ID=
DATABRICKS_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL=
DATABRICKS_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_PASSWORD=
DATABRICKS_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_OTP_SECRET=

### Snowflake
SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT=
SNOWFLAKE_CLIENT_ID=
SNOWFLAKE_CLIENT_SECRET=
SNOWFLAKE_USERNAME=
SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD=

# What gets configured
When the variables are set, the script will:

Create /etc/rstudio/databricks.conf with your workspace configuration
Create /etc/rstudio/snowflake.conf with your account configuration
Enable allow-refresh-snowflake-roles=1 and databricks-enabled=1 in /etc/rstudio/rserver.conf
Configuration is optional - services are only configured when their environment variables are present.

title: Add amd64/Windows support for wb-local containers
description:
## Summary

- Auto-detect host architecture (`arm64` / `amd64`) so wb-local containers work on both macOS (Apple Silicon) and Windows/x86 Linux without manual configuration
- Fix compatibility issues when running shell scripts from Git Bash on Windows (MINGW path conversion, CRLF line endings)
- Update npm scripts to use `bash -c` wrapper so they work cross-platform (`cmd.exe` on Windows doesn't support `./script.sh`)

## Changes

- **`docker-compose.ubuntu24.yml`** — Parameterize image names with `${ARCH_SUFFIX}` and `${IMAGE_TAG}` (defaults to `arm64:101` for backwards compatibility)
- **`run.sh`** — Auto-detect architecture via `uname -m` and export `ARCH_SUFFIX` for docker compose
- **`install-workbench.sh`** — Auto-detect architecture inside the container instead of hardcoding `arm64`
- **`connect.sh`** — Add `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` to prevent Git Bash path mangling; strip `\r` line endings after copying scripts into container
- **`package.json`** — Wrap npm scripts in `bash -c "..."` so they work on Windows (applies to both `arm:` and `wb:` scripts)
- **`README.md`** — Update title, add Windows/shell guidance, document `ARCH_SUFFIX` and `IMAGE_TAG` overrides, clarify docker login uses a GitHub token not password

## Overrides via `.env`

Users can override the auto-detected defaults:
- `ARCH_SUFFIX` — force `arm64` or `amd64`
- `IMAGE_TAG` — use a specific container image tag (e.g., `100` if `101` isn't available for amd64)

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify `./run.sh ubuntu24` + `./connect.sh` works on macOS (arm64)
- [x] Verify `./run.sh ubuntu24` + `./connect.sh` works on Windows via Git Bash (amd64)
- [x] Verify `npm run wb:start` works on both platforms
- [ ] Verify existing `arm:` npm scripts still work on macOS

title: Improve dev experience for arm-local and wb-local containers

title: Remove Quarto YAML file
description:
This `_quarto.yml` file tells Quarto that this subdirectory is a Quarto project and nothing outside of that directory matters, while the `DESCRIPTION` file indicates this is an R package. There are two good options for moving forward:

- Remove the `_quarto.yml` file and treat this like an R package, work from the root directory of this project, and expect the output HTML in a temp directory.
- Keep the YAML file and treat this like a Quarto project, work from the `quarto_basic` subdirectory (i.e. open that as the Positron workspace), and expect the HTML in the same directory as the `.qmd`.

I think either one is a fine option.
